Makefile publish: the new release-assets-check uses the overridable $(GH), but the neighbouring `gh release upload` / `gh release edit` lines still hardcode `gh`. The inconsistency is harmless today but means a fake-gh run of publish is only partial. (Out of scope; low.)
DMGVerifier.swift:144-145: in wholeDiskDevices, `dev.dropFirst("/dev/disk".count)` is evaluated twice; binding it to a local would make the compound condition easier to read. (Cosmetic.)
Makefile:352 — the GH ?= gh override applies only to release-assets-check. The upload and draft-flip steps (Makefile:341,343) still call plain `gh`. This is a minor inconsistency and not a defect.
CHANGELOG.md stops at v0.20.0 while the repo is on v0.23.6, so it is not kept in lockstep. This predates the batch and is outside its scope.

Behavior change for users who already have include_prereleases = true: the updater now reads /releases?per_page=20 instead of /releases/latest, and a list with only drafts gives updates_no_release. It is documented in README/config.example/CLAUDE.md. I did not verify whether there is a test for a stale-cache or rate-limit response in the list format.

The DMG itself (UpdateChecker.download -> HTTPClient.download) still follows redirects without a host allow-list. This predates the diff and is mitigated by the fail-closed SHA256 check and the team signature check. It could reuse the same predicate as sendBounded.
isAllowedDownloadURL (UpdateChecker.swift:373) ignores the port, so an allow-listed host on a non-standard port is accepted. Low risk (https only).
